subject: Urgent: Convexity throughput collapse causing 5xxs — exec coordination
messages:
From: Samir Shah <samir@convexity.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Becky Li <becky@convexity.ai>
Date: Thu, 27 Jul 2028 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Autocomplete API -> sudden throughput collapse, 5xx spike

Grace —

We're seeing a severe outage on our autocomplete endpoint that started ~15:40 PDT. A lot of traffic is getting 500s and latency is spiking to 6–12s for successful requests. This started right after we pushed a small model prompt tweak, but we rolled that back and the error rate stayed high.

Attached is a short snapshot (PNG) of 1-min error rate and a CSV of the token/time series. Peak error rate is ~18% on our peak shard, and the 95th latency moved from ~200ms to ~3.1s. This is impacting search relevance for customers and a few downstream batch jobs are timing out.

We requested support via the console and opened a ticket but need an exec-level contact and a war-room — the account team is on standby and customers are asking for an ETA.

Can Redwood triage immediately? We need visibility on root cause (routing, model variant, or infra) and a recovery plan.

— Samir
Head of Engineering, Convexity
[Attachment: convexity-error-snapshot-20280727.png (PNG, 220KB)]
[Attachment: convexity-kpi-timeseries-0727.csv (CSV, 230KB)]
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Shah <samir@convexity.ai>, Becky Li <becky@convexity.ai>

Subject: Re: Autocomplete API -> sudden throughput collapse, 5xx spike

Samir — thank you for the fast heads-up and the attachments.

Acked: we're standing up a focused war-room and will triage immediately. High-level plan:
- 16:30 PDT: short triage call (15m) to confirm scope and assign leads (SRE, model, routing).
- Post-triage: immediate mitigations (reroute traffic to fallback model variant, throttle noncritical routes, temporary client-side backoff guidance).
- Hourly cadence: customer status update and internal exec summary.

Please join the triage call if you can — link below. Our SRE lead (Rishi) will take first stab at logs/metrics, Aditya will coordinate engineering-level resource prioritization, Marissa will draft the customer-facing summary, and I'll own exec comms.

War-room call: https://meet.redwood.ai/j/warroom-convexity-0728

I'll follow up after the triage with an initial snapshot and concrete mitigations.

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Samir Shah <samir@convexity.ai>, Becky Li <becky@convexity.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 27 Jul 2028 16:55:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Autocomplete API -> sudden throughput collapse, 5xx spike

Team — quick triage notes from the war-room (summary):

Observations (first 30m):
- Error class: ~92% are 5xx backend timeouts originating from the inference pool serving Convexity's model variant.
- Scope: impact concentrated on two inference shards (us-west-2 GPU pool) — not global.
- Telemetry: sudden increase in KV-cache misses correlated with longer generation times; batch sizes for requests on the affected pool jumped from median 4 -> 14 in a short window.

Preliminary hypothesis:
- A downstream client-side change increased burstiness (larger batch submissions and short inter-request gaps), causing inefficient scheduling and larger effective batch sizes. This increases per-batch latency and leads to queue saturation and timeouts.

Immediate mitigations applied (16:45 PDT):
- Scoped traffic reroute: moved 40% of Convexity traffic to standby model variant (quantized), which reduced 5xx rate on that cohort by ~9 percentage points in the first 10m.
- Autoscaler override: forced immediate scale-out of two extra nodes in affected pool (approx +25% capacity).
- Short-term rate-limiter: applied per-customer token throttle for non-critical routes to relieve tail pressure.

Next steps (tactical):
- Engineering (Aditya): confirm if any scheduling kernel or runtime change was pushed in the past 24h.
- Product/SRE (me): collect detailed per-request batch histograms and KV-cache miss traces (pushing logs to the shared drive).
- CS (Marissa): coordinate the customer-facing update and field expectation on ETA.

I'll circulate the logs snapshot and a short timeline in Drive (link below). If traffic pattern doesn't normalize in 60m we'll consider full traffic migration to standby cluster and a more aggressive throttling policy.

Logs/diag: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/convexity-incident-0728
Attachments: [sre-initial-logs-0728.txt]

— Rishi
Senior SRE — Redwood Inference
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 27 Jul 2028 17:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Autocomplete API -> sudden throughput collapse, 5xx spike — exec summary and asks

Team — quick executive summary and explicit asks for the next 2 hours:

What happened (one-liner): conv-batch burst caused scheduling inefficiency -> queue saturation -> timeout 5xx spike on two us-west-2 shards.
What we've done: partial reroute to standby model (40%), emergency scale-out (+25% nodes), applied per-customer noncritical throttles.
Current status: 5xxs down to ~5% overall (from 18% peak) on the mixed cohort; tail latency still elevated for a subset of requests.

Asks:
- CS (Marissa): prepare a single-page customer status note summarizing what happened, what we did, and firm ETA for full recovery (target: 2 hours). Use conservative language and call out mitigations done. Laura, please review for contractual language.
- SRE (Rishi): provide a 60-min timeline and the post-mortem owner. Identify whether we need a change to scheduling/backpressure behavior in the runtime.
- Eng (Grace): loop in any execs at Convexity if requested; keep me posted on escalations.

I'll be available for exec brief at 18:00 PDT if needed. If the mitigation trajectory stalls, we will escalate to full traffic migration to the standby cluster and temporary routing by approximate latency SLO.

— Aditya
VP Engineering — Redwood Inference
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Shah <samir@convexity.ai>, Becky Li <becky@convexity.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 28 Jul 2028 11:23:00 -0700
Subject: Convexity incident update — stabilized, next 24h plan and customer note

Samir / Becky —

Short update from the war-room: the incident is currently stabilized and error rates have returned to baseline across your traffic after the interventions described below.

What we observed: brief burst of large request batches that increased effective scheduling sizes and KV-cache misses on two us-west-2 shards. That triggered queue growth and 5xx timeouts for a subset of requests.

What we did (tactical recap):
- 40% traffic rerouted to a verified standby model variant (lower precision) — immediate reduction in 5xx for that cohort.
- Emergency autoscaler forced +2 nodes in affected pool and temporary conservative throttles for non-critical routes.
- We applied a short-lived per-customer throughput cap on the ingestion endpoint and coordinated with your team to smooth request bursts.

Customer-facing note (summary):
We experienced a transient increase in backend timeouts affecting autocomplete. Our engineering team applied reroutes and increased capacity; error rates have returned to normal. We are continuing to monitor and will publish a full post-incident report within 72 hours.

Next 24h plan (owners):
- SRE (Rishi): collect and analyze batch histograms, KV-cache traces; deliver timeline and root-cause hypotheses (ETA: 24h).
- Eng (Aditya): evaluate scheduler/backpressure adjustments and whether a runtime patch or configuration change is required (ETA: 48–72h).
- CS (Marissa): send vetted customer note and follow up with key Convexity stakeholders (ETA: 30m — see draft below).

Draft customer note (please feel free to adapt):
—
Hi Samir / Becky —
We wanted to let you know that an incident earlier impacted autocomplete traffic. Our team identified the cause and implemented routing and capacity mitigations; your traffic has returned to normal. We will share a full post-incident report that includes timeline, root cause, and remediation steps within 72 hours. If you need a dedicated postmortem call, we can schedule one.
—

Please confirm whether you want a postmortem call. If there are any compliance/reporting requirements for the incident, let us know and we'll include those in the report.

Thanks again for your partnership and patience. We'll keep you updated via this thread and adhoc briefings.

— Grace
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
